context:
Create a type probing script that connects to a pg_mooncake instance and
attempts CREATE TABLE ... USING columnstore for each standard SQL type.
Record success/failure per type per pg_mooncake version. Output a structured
YAML/JSON matrix. Optionally add a _map_column_types() override to
PgMooncakeAdapter that consults the matrix and emits warnings for
unsupported types before DDL execution.

Reference: PgMooncakeAdapter._add_columnstore_access_method() in
benchbox/platforms/pg_mooncake.py already transforms DDL - type mapping
would slot in alongside it in create_schema().
description:
pg_mooncake's columnstore access method silently drops or rejects certain
PostgreSQL data types (e.g., SERIAL, arrays, composite types). BenchBox
currently inherits all type handling from PostgreSQLAdapter with no
pg_mooncake-specific validation - unsupported types fail at CREATE TABLE
time with opaque PostgreSQL errors.

A compatibility matrix would:
1. Document which SQL types columnstore supports per pg_mooncake version
2. Enable BenchBox to warn or map types before DDL execution
3. Guide future benchmark schema design for pg_mooncake

pg_mooncake is actively evolving; type support changes across releases.
The matrix should be version-tagged and ideally generated via automated
type probing rather than manually maintained.

Split from pg-extension-advanced-benchmarking (originally deferred from
pg-mooncake-platform-adapter, completed 2026-02-15).

anti_patterns.instead: use version-tagged probing or configuration instead
anti_patterns.why: pg_mooncake's supported types change across releases
users need to know which columns won't work
